h1: The Quarter Ari by UHG — a sky-high boutique hotel in the heart of Ari where you sleep above the city atop Ari Hills
intro: Picture this: you wake up, pull back the curtains, and Bangkok stretches out below you from twenty-something floors up; come evening you head up to the sky bar for a drink with the city lights as your backdrop, then drop down the elevator and you're walking Ari's cafés and great little restaurants within minutes — The Quarter Ari by UHG is a boutique hotel under UHG that sits on floors 22 to 34 of the Ari Hills building on Phahonyothin Road, right in the heart of Ari · what most people talk about is the rooftop pool and the Hilltops sky bar with their city views, paired with service that feels warmer than the price · around 150 rooms, from about ฿1,800/night, scored 9.0 from 1,440 reviews on Trip.com

body.html: Who The Quarter Ari is for — the shortest way to put it: The Quarter Ari by UHG is a boutique hotel for people who want to stay in the heart of Ari — the neighborhood Bangkokians point to as the city's hub of cafés, restaurants, and young-crowd lifestyle — while still getting a sky-high room with city views and a rooftop pool on a budget they can actually justify · it isn't a five-star luxury hotel by the river selling grandeur, and it isn't a budget hostel, but a 4-star boutique hotel set on floors 22 to 34 of the Ari Hills building on Phahonyothin Road, so nearly every room gets a high view and plenty of natural light · it's part of UHG, a group known for its personal, attentive service · it's still open and doing well: TripAdvisor gave it a Travelers' Choice 2026 award and ranks it near the top in the Phaya Thai area · real reviews line up on this — the people it suits best are couples, solo travelers mixing work and travel, and small families who want a central-city location with a good view, more than those after a large suite-sized room or every amenity of a chain hotel · another group that says they loved it: international travelers who want to experience Bangkok like a local, in a neighborhood where Thais actually live rather than a purely touristy one · in short, it's a hotel that plays the 'high view + city-dweller location' angle just right, at a price that's hard to match

Location and getting around — this is the part to understand correctly before you book · The Quarter Ari sits on Phahonyothin Road, on the side near Soi 10, in Phaya Thai district, about an 8-minute walk from BTS Ari (roughly 600–700 meters), which is an easy walk on a nice day but isn't step-out-the-door close to the station — a detail many reviews stress is worth knowing, especially if you're dragging heavy bags or arriving in strong sun · the upside is that once you're on the BTS, Ari connects straight onto the Sukhumvit line into Siam, Asok, and across the rest of the city without changing lines · within walking distance the hotel is surrounded by the best of Ari — cafés, specialty coffee shops, both Thai and international restaurants, small markets, and dessert spots Bangkokians travel for · TripAdvisor scores the neighborhood's walkability at around 81 out of 100, which is high for Bangkok · for longer trips: Siam/Sam Yan is about 15–20 min by car or a few BTS stops, Chatuchak and the railway park are very close, and importantly Don Muang (DMK) airport is easier to reach than Suvarnabhumi because it's on the north side of the city · one thing to note is that Phahonyothin Road gets congested during rush hour, so if you call a Grab in the evening allow extra time, and the Ari Hills building itself is an office/mixed-use tower with the actual hotel lobby on an upper floor reached by elevator — the first time you may be a little unsure which floor to check in on

"Pulled back the curtains in the morning to the whole city laid out below from twenty-something floors up, and it instantly felt worth what I paid · about an eight-minute walk to BTS Ari, in exchange for staying in a neighborhood packed with great cafés — totally fine by me."

Room types and decor — The Quarter Ari has around 150 rooms spread across floors 22 to 34, split into several tiers · it starts with the Superior Room at roughly 25 sqm, a compact entry-level room but well laid out, with a King or Twin bed, good for solo travelers or couples who use the room just to sleep after a full day out · step up to the Deluxe Room at roughly 35 sqm, clearly more spacious, with a Deluxe with Bathtub version for those who like a soak · the largest is the Premium Room at roughly 39 sqm, with the most space and the best view angle · the decor is warm contemporary, leaning on woodwork and earth-tone fabrics, clean-looking and uncluttered · the thing every review agrees on is the large windows and city views from the high floors, which make the rooms feel airy and more special than the price suggests · every room has a flat-screen TV, a coffee/tea maker, a minibar, a safe, free drinking water, and a bathroom with good-quality amenities · many reviews praise the comfortable beds, how quiet the rooms are up above the street noise, and how lovely the morning light is · for people here to work, the desk and stable Wi-Fi also earn praise · one small tip: if the view matters to you, ask for a high floor or a city-facing side when you book, because some lower rooms or ones facing into the building don't get the full view

Facilities, pool, and gym — the most talked-about highlight of The Quarter Ari is the rooftop pool with city views, which many reviews describe as an infinity-edge pool looking out across a wide stretch of the Bangkok skyline · late afternoon into the evening is the popular time for guests to head up for a dip, take photos, and sit out in the breeze · above the pool is the Hilltops sky bar, which has become the hotel's standout feature — good atmosphere, lovely views, perfect for a drink in the evening watching the sunset and the city lights · on the wellness side there's a modern Urban Fit gym and a steam room to unwind after a full day of walking · there's also an airport drop-off service, laundry service, in-building parking, and free Wi-Fi throughout · to be straight about it, the rooftop pool is more about atmosphere and the view than a long lap pool for serious swimming, and the common areas aren't resort-sized — but for the feel of being sky-high in the middle of the city, it does this better than the price would suggest at the 4-star level

Food and bar — the hotel's main restaurant is Hilly's, an all-day dining spot serving Thai and international food that also handles breakfast for guests · the breakfast menu offers Western, Asian, and Thai options · we'll be honest, per the real reviews: breakfast is where opinions split — plenty of guests praise it and say it gets the day off to a good start, while some reviews say the selection isn't huge and on some mornings the ingredients weren't as fresh as hoped · it's worth setting expectations accordingly, and the upside is that the location helps a lot, because just down the elevator and out the door you're surrounded by Ari's famous cafés and restaurants, so many people choose to head out for breakfast or other meals to soak up the neighborhood's character · as for the Hilltops sky bar, that's the star on the drinks side — sipping a cocktail or wine in the evening with the city view is good enough that many reviews call it the main reason they chose to stay here · overall, the in-hotel food is a decent-to-good extra, but the real charm of staying here is using the hotel as a base to go eat your way around Ari

Service — service is where the praise is thickest in the real reviews, and a big reason the overall score runs high · several front-desk and F&B staff get named and thanked personally, again and again — there's a front-desk staffer that guests of many nationalities mention for their attentiveness, remembering guests, and giving personalized tips on places to eat and visit, plus the restaurant team and a manager that many reviews say 'went above and beyond' · helpful check-in, calling cars, booking restaurants, and answering travelers' questions leave many guests feeling they got warmer service than a 4-star price would suggest · but to be fair, a few voices in the reviews say the front desk's response can be slower than it should be at certain times, especially when guests are checking in and out at once or when the hotel is full, and a few were confused about the building's floors/elevators at first · overall, service is still a clear strength here

What real reviews say (both praise and gripes) — pulling from Trip.com, Booking.com, and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: the city views from the high floors are stunning both from the rooms and from the pool, the rooftop pool and Hilltops sky bar have a great evening atmosphere, the rooms are clean and quiet thanks to the height, the beds are comfortable, the staff are friendly and especially attentive, the Ari location lets you walk to cafés and great restaurants, and it's good value given the view and service you get · on the watch-out side: the most frequently mentioned is the divisive breakfast, with some reviews saying the selection isn't large or the ingredients weren't as fresh as hoped · next is the roughly 8-minute walk to BTS Ari, which some feel is farther than expected, especially in strong sun or with luggage; cleanliness, where a few guests occasionally found towels or sheets with a musty smell and hair/ants in the room; the air conditioning in some common areas not being cold enough; and the confusion over the building's elevators/floors on first check-in · most of these gripes can be sorted out by choosing the right room, setting expectations correctly, and asking about the way up in advance, rather than being major problems that keep people from coming back

"The staff were so lovely — they recommended cafés and restaurants in Ari and we ended up trying several great spots · the one downside was the limited breakfast selection, so we mostly went out — which was actually fun, since this neighborhood is full of standout places."

Price comparison and value — the starting price for a Superior Room is around ฿1,800/night at normal rates (about US$52 as shown on Trip.com), and can climb to around ฿2,800–3,500+ in high season or over long weekends · larger rooms like the Deluxe and Premium run from around ฿2,500 up depending on size and timing · compared with hotels that have a rooftop pool and a city-view sky bar in central Bangkok, most of which price well above this, The Quarter Ari feels like strong value among affordable high-view hotels, especially once you count the city views from floor 22 up, the rooftop pool, the sky bar, and the warm service · if you plan to live in the Ari neighborhood, walking to cafés and great restaurants every day, plus heading up for the pool and a sky-bar drink in the evening, every baht you spend earns its keep · for those who want a large suite-sized room or every amenity of a big chain hotel, you may need to compare options at a higher budget

What to know before you book — a few things help make the stay smoother · one, the hotel is on floors 22–34 of the Ari Hills building, a mixed-use tower, so ask about the way up and the check-in floor in advance and allow a little extra time when you first arrive · two, if the view matters, ask for a high floor or a city-facing side when you book · three, it's about an 8-minute walk to BTS Ari, so if you're dragging heavy bags or arriving in strong sun, consider a short ride or the hotel's service · four, set expectations on breakfast and plan to head out for Ari's food as your main option · five, in Bangkok's high season (November–February) prices rise quickly, so book ahead, compare across platforms, and choose free cancellation if your plans aren't firm yet

Summary — from all the real reviews, The Quarter Ari by UHG is the hotel that suits people who want a sky-high city-view stay in the heart of Ari on a reachable budget, with a rooftop pool, a sky bar, and warm service best · the views from floor 22 up, the rooftop pool, the Hilltops sky bar, and a location where you can walk to Ari's cafés and great restaurants every day make it good value that's hard to match at the same price · if you want a large suite-sized room, a flawless upscale breakfast, or a hotel where you step out the door and you're at the BTS, this may not be the answer, and you should look at a big chain hotel right by a Skytrain station instead · but for a city trip where you want a high view, a sky-high atmosphere, and the charm of Ari as Bangkokians actually live it, with the attentive service of the UHG group — The Quarter Ari answers that almost perfectly, which is why it keeps a high score and ongoing Travelers' Choice recognition

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Quarter Ari by UHG

faq.q: Where is The Quarter Ari by UHG · is it a long walk to the BTS?
faq.a: The hotel is on floors 22–34 of the Ari Hills building on Phahonyothin Road, Phaya Thai district, in the heart of Ari · it's about an 8-minute walk from BTS Ari (roughly 600–700 meters), not right at the station but an easy walk · all around it are Ari's cafés and restaurants · easy BTS connections into Siam/Asok

faq.q: Does The Quarter Ari have a swimming pool and a sky bar?
faq.a: Yes — there's a rooftop pool with city views and the Hilltops sky bar that many reviews call a standout — sit for an evening drink over the city lights with a great atmosphere · there's also an Urban Fit gym and a steam room

faq.q: What's the starting price at The Quarter Ari · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start from around ฿1,800/night for a Superior Room of about 25 sqm at normal rates · there are Deluxe and Deluxe with Bathtub rooms of about 35 sqm, and a Premium Room of about 39 sqm for those who want a larger room and the best view angle · high-season prices (Nov–Feb) rise fast, so compare across platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is The Quarter Ari for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, solo travelers, and small families who want a sky-high city-view stay in the heart of Ari on a reachable budget, who like a rooftop pool, a sky bar, and walking to the neighborhood's cafés and great restaurants · if you're after a large suite-sized room or a hotel right at the BTS, a big chain hotel in another area may suit you better

faq.q: What's breakfast like at The Quarter Ari?
faq.a: Breakfast is included in the room rate and served at Hilly's restaurant, all-day dining with both Thai and international menus · per the real reviews, opinions on breakfast are fairly divided — some praise it, others say the selection isn't large or the ingredients weren't as fresh as expected · the upside is that the surrounding Ari neighborhood has plenty of standout cafés and restaurants to head out to

faq.q: What's the building like · which floor do you check in on?
faq.a: The Quarter Ari is on floors 22–34 of the Ari Hills building, a mixed-use tower rather than a pure hotel building · the lobby and front desk are on an upper floor reached by elevator · the first time it can be a little confusing about the elevators/floors, so we recommend asking about the way up in advance and allowing time when you arrive
